title: A `Using:` written as an indented pipeline instead of a lambda
description:
`All Pairs` searches the *current value*, so over a List<List<Int>> it would
pair whole rows against each other. Writing Map Each's `Using:` as a pipeline
runs that pipeline in the lambda's place, once per row with the row as its

expression layer has no way to iterate. A body stands in for any 1-parameter
`Using:` lambda, not just Map Each's: `Filter`, `Sort By`, `Group By` and the
rest take one too.

Each row here holds exactly one evenly-divisible pair (AoC 2017 day 2 part
2). The body finds it and divides it; the outer pipeline sums the results.

title: Local bindings: naming a value for one stage's expressions
description:
The lambda below needs the mean of the whole list, which no lambda can reach
on its own — it sees one element at a time. `Consider mean Of …` computes it
once from the value entering the stage and binds it by name for every
expression on that stage.

The preposition says where a binding's value comes from, and it has to: a
1-parameter lambda already means two different things in Domain depending on
where it is written (per element in a `Using:`, once over the current value
in a measured argument like `Size:`), and a binding has no slot to say which.
So `As` never sees the pipeline value — it binds a constant or a function —
and `Of` always does.

The two `As` bindings cost nothing at all: `tolerance` folds into the lambda
as a literal and `spread` is inlined at its call site, so both are gone
before either backend sees the program.

title: A first-class graph: parse an edge list once, then ask it several questions
description:
Before Graph<K> an explicit graph had nowhere to live. BFS and Dijkstra took
a Grid, so they only reached geometry; Explore takes a successor lambda, so
its graph is implicit and cannot be built once and queried twice; and
Topological Sort's adjacency map had to be rebuilt at every stage and had
nowhere to put a weight. `Convert To Graph` gives the parse somewhere to go.

The roads are undirected, which is one arc each way — `Mode: Undirected` is
how you say that, rather than a second kind of value.

`Shortest Path` answers which way rather than how far: the cheapest route
from London to Exeter is via Bristol (118 + 84 = 202), not via Oxford
(57 + 74 + 84 = 215), even though both are three cities.

title: Conway's Game of Life — a glider on an infinite plane, run 4 generations

title: Hide and seek — several players in one room, and a network in between
description:
The rule this game is here to demonstrate is the one in game/net.go: **one
request is in flight per tag, and firing again supersedes the one that was
out.** A position poll is exactly the tag that wants it. HTTP replies can
arrive out of order, and a client polling at 2 Hz against a server that
sometimes takes half a second will, under any unbounded scheme, receive an
answer from three polls ago *after* a newer one and merge it — which shows up
as other players teleporting backwards, reads as a game bug rather than a
networking one, and costs a day to find.

So the timer fires without asking whether one is already out. What that costs
is a dropped reply, and what a dropped reply looks like is `age`: the number
of syncs since the last answer. A slow room degrades into a **stale frame**,
drawn dim and labelled, rather than into a stall.
source:
# Hide and seek — several players in one room, and a network in between.
#
# The rule this game is here to demonstrate is the one in game/net.go: **one
# request is in flight per tag, and firing again supersedes the one that was
# out.** A position poll is exactly the tag that wants it. HTTP replies can
# arrive out of order, and a client polling at 2 Hz against a server that
# sometimes takes half a second will, under any unbounded scheme, receive an
# answer from three polls ago *after* a newer one and merge it — which shows up
# as other players teleporting backwards, reads as a game bug rather than a
# networking one, and costs a day to find.
#
# So the timer fires without asking whether one is already out. What that costs
# is a dropped reply, and what a dropped reply looks like is `age`: the number
# of syncs since the last answer. A slow room degrades into a **stale frame**,
# drawn dim and labelled, rather than into a stall.

Innate Domain: Game Dev

Cursed Object: myName As "fox"
Cursed Object: room As "https://hide.example/room/pine"
Cursed Object: boardCols As 15

Part World:
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> {board: list(
                "...............",
                "..####....###..",
                "..#..........#.",
                "..#...####...#.",
                "......#..#.....",
                ".####.#..#.....",
                "..............."),
            lines: emptylist(""),
            me: point(6, 1), step: point(0, 0), others: emptylist({name: "", r: 0, c: 0, it: 1 = 0}),
            age: 0, caught: 1 = 0, note: "arrows move, q leaves"}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Moving. A wall is a wall whatever the room thinks.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Part Entity "Step":
    # `step` is where the player wants to go; this is where they end up.
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) ->
            consider p as padd(w.me, w.step)
            in if prow(p) < 0 or prow(p) > 6 or pcol(p) < 0 or pcol(p) >= boardCols
                or charat(item(w.board, prow(p)), pcol(p)) = "#"
                then w
                else with(w, "me", p)

Part On "key up":
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> with(w, "step", point(-1, 0))
    Shikigami: Step

Part On "key down":
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> with(w, "step", point(1, 0))
    Shikigami: Step

Part On "key left":
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> with(w, "step", point(0, -1))
    Shikigami: Step

Part On "key right":
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> with(w, "step", point(0, 1))
    Shikigami: Step

Part On "key q":
    Simple Domain: Quit

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The sync
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Part Every 400:
    # No `pending` guard, and that is the point: a newer position is worth more
    # than an older answer, so the new request supersedes the old one.
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> with(w, "age", w.age + 1)
    Domain Expansion: Request
        Url: (w) -> room + "/sync"
        Method: "POST"
        Body: (w) -> tojson({name: myName, r: prow(w.me), c: pcol(w.me)})
        As: "world"
        Into: {players: List < {name: Text, r: Int, c: Int, it: Bool} >, closing: Bool}
        Timeout: 900

Part Reply "world":
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        # Three views of one answer, each naming what it wants: everybody else,
        # and where the seekers are standing.
        Consider seen Of
            Cursed Technique: Apply
                Using: (w) -> reply.value.players
            Cursed Technique: Filter
                Using: (p) -> not(p.name = myName)
        Consider hunters Of
            Cursed Technique: Apply
                Using: (w) -> reply.value.players
            Cursed Technique: Filter
                Using: (p) -> p.it and not(p.name = myName)
            Cursed Technique: Map Each
                Using: (p) -> point(p.r, p.c)
        Using: (w) ->
            if not(reply.ok)
                then with(w, "note", "the room is quiet (" + reply.error + ")")
                else with(with(with(with(w, "others", seen), "age", 0),
                        "caught", w.caught or contains(hunters, w.me)),
                    "note", if contains(hunters, w.me)
                        then "caught"
                        else totext(length(seen)) + " other(s) in the room")

Part Draw:
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> with(w, "lines", w.board)
    Simple Domain: For k in range(6)
        Cursed Technique: Apply
            Using: (w, k) ->
                if k >= length(w.others)
                    then w
                    else consider p as item(w.others, k)
                        in consider row as item(w.lines, p.r)
                        in with(w, "lines", set(w.lines, p.r, withchar(row, p.c, if p.it then "!" else "o")))
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) ->
            consider row as item(w.lines, prow(w.me))
            in with(w, "lines", set(w.lines, prow(w.me), withchar(row, pcol(w.me), "@")))
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) ->
            # A frame the room has not confirmed is drawn dim and says how old
            # it is. The game keeps running on it — a stale picture is a much
            # better answer than a stopped one.
            stack(
                beside(style(text("HIDE AND SEEK"), "bold"), text("   you are "), style(text("@"), "bold cyan")),
                (if w.age > 1
                    then style(box(draw(w.lines)), "dim")
                    else box(draw(w.lines))),
                text(if w.age > 1 then "stale — " + totext(w.age) + " syncs since the room answered" else w.note))

Part Ending:
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> if w.caught then "caught" else "still hidden"
    Reveal: stdout

# Hide and seek, with the room played by this file. Every `reply world` line
# is one answer from the server; the gaps between them are what a slow room
# looks like from inside the game.

key right            # move, then let the timer poll
key right
tick
reply world {"players": [{"name":"fox","r":6,"c":3,"it":false},{"name":"hare","r":4,"c":9,"it":false},{"name":"owl","r":2,"c":5,"it":true}], "closing": false}
frame                # two others in the room, and `!` is the one who is it

tick                 # two polls with no answer: the picture goes stale rather

reply world {"players": [{"name":"fox","r":6,"c":3,"it":false},{"name":"owl","r":5,"c":3,"it":true}], "closing": false}

Snake and tetris are boards. This one is a **state machine**: the world holds

source:
# Oregon — a game with no grid at all.
#
# Snake and tetris are boards. This one is a **state machine**: the world holds
# a `scene`, every other Part asks which scene it is in, and the picture is
# text. It is here to check that the scope carries a game whose interesting
# part is choices rather than cells — menus, resources, and a day that can go
# wrong on its own.
#
# The menu is derived rather than typed twice. `Part Entity "Menu":` is the one
# place that says what a scene offers, and every Part that changes the scene
# calls it by name afterwards.

Innate Domain: Game Dev

Cursed Object: goal As 200

Part World:
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> {scene: "trail", shown: "", menu: emptylist(""), lines: emptylist(""), cursor: 0, day: 1, mile: 0, food: 120, money: 60, oxen: 2, health: 5, leaving: 1 = 0, note: "The wagon is loaded. Oregon is 200 miles west."}

Part Start:
    Shikigami: Menu

Part Entity "Menu":
    # scene -> what may be chosen. Written once, called after every change.
    # The highlight goes back to the top when the scene does change, and stays
    # where it was when it did not: `shown` is what the menu was last built
    # for, which is the only way to tell those two apart from in here.
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) ->
            consider m as (if w.scene = "trail"
                    then list("Push on west", "Rest a day", "Stop at the fort")
                    else if w.scene = "fort"
                    then list("Buy 20 food - 10 coin", "Buy an ox - 25 coin", "Back to the trail")
                    else if w.scene = "moving"
                    then list("Make camp")
                    else list("Leave"))
            in with(with(with(w, "menu", m), "shown", w.scene),
                "cursor", if w.scene = w.shown and w.cursor < length(m) then w.cursor else 0)

Part On "key up":
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> with(w, "cursor", clamp(w.cursor - 1, 0, length(w.menu) - 1))

Part On "key down":
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> with(w, "cursor", clamp(w.cursor + 1, 0, length(w.menu) - 1))

Part On "key enter":
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) ->
            if w.scene = "trail"
                then (if w.cursor = 0
                    then with(w, "scene", "moving")
                    else if w.cursor = 1
                    then with(with(with(with(w, "day", w.day + 1), "food", w.food - 4), "health", clamp(w.health + 1, 0, 5)), "note", "A day in camp. Everyone is steadier for it.")
                    else with(w, "scene", "fort"))
            else if w.scene = "fort"
                then (if w.cursor = 0 and w.money >= 10
                    then with(with(with(w, "money", w.money - 10), "food", w.food + 20), "note", "Twenty pounds of flour, and a shorter purse.")
                    else if w.cursor = 1 and w.money >= 25
                    then with(with(with(w, "money", w.money - 25), "oxen", w.oxen + 1), "note", "A fresh ox. The wagon will keep up now.")
                    else if w.cursor = 2
                    then with(w, "scene", "trail")
                    else with(w, "note", "Not enough coin for that."))
            else if w.scene = "moving"
                then with(with(w, "scene", "trail"), "note", "You make camp for the night.")
            else with(w, "leaving", 1 = 1)
    Shikigami: Menu
    # The last scene has one thing on its menu, and this is what it does.
    Simple Domain: Quit
        Using: (w) -> w.leaving

Part On "key q":
    Simple Domain: Quit

# A day on the move: distance, hunger, and whatever the trail decides.
Part Every 600:
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) ->
            if not(w.scene = "moving")
                then w
                else consider far as 6 + w.oxen * 3 + random(7)
                    in consider eaten as 4 + w.oxen
                    in with(with(with(with(w, "day", w.day + 1), "mile", w.mile + far), "food", w.food - eaten), "note", "You make " + totext(far) + " miles.")

    # The trail's own opinion. One day in three has something to say.
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) ->
            if not(w.scene = "moving") or random(3) > 0
                then w
                else consider what as random(4)
                    in if what = 0
                        then with(with(w, "food", w.food - 15), "note", "A river crossing. Fifteen pounds of food went downstream.")
                        else if what = 1
                        then with(with(w, "health", clamp(w.health - 1, 0, 5)), "note", "Fever in the wagon. Somebody is not well.")
                        else if what = 2
                        then with(with(w, "food", w.food + 25), "note", "Good hunting. Twenty-five pounds of meat.")
                        else with(with(w, "money", w.money + 12), "note", "A trader pays twelve coin for a spare wheel.")

    # Hunger costs health, and health runs out.
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) ->
            if w.food >= 0
                then w
                else with(with(with(w, "food", 0), "health", clamp(w.health - 1, 0, 5)), "note", "Nothing left to eat. " + w.note)

    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) ->
            if w.mile >= goal
                then with(with(w, "scene", "arrived"), "note", "Oregon, on day " + totext(w.day) + ".")
                else if w.health <= 0
                then with(with(w, "scene", "lost"), "note", "The wagon stops for good on day " + totext(w.day) + ".")
                else w
    Shikigami: Menu

Part Draw:
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> with(w, "lines", emptylist(""))
    Simple Domain: For k in range(3)
        Cursed Technique: Apply
            Using: (w, k) ->
                if k >= length(w.menu)
                    then w

title: Snake — the first game, and the smallest one that is a game
description:
The board lives in the world as a `Sparse` plane, and the snake moves by
painting two cells: the new head, and the tail it left behind. That is the
whole trick, and it is why the board never has to be rebuilt from the body:
a frame is `draw(w.plane)`, one call.

A `Sparse` reports the bounding box of the cells that have been set, so the
two corners set below are what fix the board's size. Everything inside them
reads the default "." until something is painted there.

Eating rings the terminal bell — `Simple Domain: Beep`, guarded so a step
that both eats and dies (the head lands on the food square exactly where the
wall or the tail was going to end the game anyway) does not sound one for a
game that is already over.

# Snake — the first game, and the smallest one that is a game.
#
# The board lives in the world as a `Sparse` plane, and the snake moves by
# painting two cells: the new head, and the tail it left behind. That is the
# whole trick, and it is why the board never has to be rebuilt from the body:
# a frame is `draw(w.plane)`, one call.
#
# A `Sparse` reports the bounding box of the cells that have been set, so the
# two corners set below are what fix the board's size. Everything inside them
# reads the default "." until something is painted there.
#
# Eating rings the terminal bell — `Simple Domain: Beep`, guarded so a step
# that both eats and dies (the head lands on the food square exactly where the
# wall or the tail was going to end the game anyway) does not sound one for a
# game that is already over.

Innate Domain: Game Dev

Cursed Object: lastRow As 7
Cursed Object: lastCol As 11

Part World:
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> {plane: put(put(sparse("."), 0, 0, "."), lastRow, lastCol, "."), body: list(point(4, 5), point(4, 4), point(4, 3)), dir: point(0, 1), food: point(2, 9), score: 0, over: 1 = 0}

# The snake and its first meal, painted once before the first frame.
Part Start:
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) ->
            consider painted as put(put(put(w.plane, 4, 5, "o"), 4, 4, "o"), 4, 3, "o")
            in with(w, "plane", put(painted, prow(w.food), pcol(w.food), "*"))

# Four keys, one direction each. A snake cannot turn back on itself, so a
# reversal is ignored rather than fatal — the arrow key that would kill you is
# the one people press by accident.
Part On "key up":
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> if prow(w.dir) = 1 then w else with(w, "dir", point(-1, 0))

Part On "key down":
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> if prow(w.dir) = -1 then w else with(w, "dir", point(1, 0))

Part On "key left":
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> if pcol(w.dir) = 1 then w else with(w, "dir", point(0, -1))

Part On "key right":
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> if pcol(w.dir) = -1 then w else with(w, "dir", point(0, 1))

Part On "key q":
    Simple Domain: Quit

# One step, in three stages. A Part's body is an ordinary pipeline, so the
# stages in between may be any shape they like — only the last one has to be
# the world again.
#
# Death freezes rather than quits. `Simple Domain: Quit` ends the program where
# it happens, so quitting on the fatal step would mean the player never sees
# the board that killed them: the last frame drawn would be the one before it.
# A game over is a state the world is in, and `q` is what leaves.
Part Every 150:
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> {w: w, head: padd(first(w.body), w.dir)}
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (s) -> {w: s.w, head: s.head, eat: s.head = s.w.food, dead: prow(s.head) < 0 or prow(s.head) > lastRow or pcol(s.head) < 0 or pcol(s.head) > lastCol or contains(s.w.body, s.head)}
    Simple Domain: Beep
        Using: (s) -> s.eat and not(s.w.over)
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (s) ->
            if s.w.over
                then s.w
                else if s.dead
                then with(s.w, "over", 1 = 1)
                else consider grown as concat(list(s.head), s.w.body)
                    in consider body as (if s.eat then grown else take(grown, length(s.w.body)))
                    in consider tail as last(s.w.body)
                    in consider food as (if s.eat then point(random(lastRow + 1), random(lastCol + 1)) else s.w.food)
                    in consider laid as put(s.w.plane, prow(s.head), pcol(s.head), "o")
                    in consider swept as (if s.eat then put(laid, prow(food), pcol(food), "*") else put(laid, prow(tail), pcol(tail), "."))
                    in {plane: swept, body: body, dir: s.w.dir, food: food, score: s.w.score + (if s.eat then 1 else 0), over: 1 = 0}

Part Draw:
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) ->
            stack(
                beside(text("score "), style(text(totext(w.score)), "bold yellow")),
                box(draw(w.plane)),
                text(if w.over then "game over" else "arrows move, q quits"))

Part Ending:
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> "final score " + totext(w.score)
    Reveal: stdout

title: Tetris — the game that asks whether the list vocabulary carries real logic
description:
The well is a `List<Text>`, one string per row, "." empty and "#" filled.
That representation is what makes the two hard parts easy: a full row is a
row with no "." in it, and clearing one is `take` + `drop` with an empty row
put back on top.

A tetromino is four cells and nothing else, so every operation on one is a
`Simple Domain: For k in range(4)` — the loop that binds each lap as an
ambient parameter while threading the world through. That is what lets the
same four-cell walk be written once, as a `Part Entity`, and called by name
from a key handler, from the timer and from the frame.
source:
# Tetris — the game that asks whether the list vocabulary carries real logic.
#
# The well is a `List<Text>`, one string per row, "." empty and "#" filled.
# That representation is what makes the two hard parts easy: a full row is a
# row with no "." in it, and clearing one is `take` + `drop` with an empty row
# put back on top.
#
# A tetromino is four cells and nothing else, so every operation on one is a
# `Simple Domain: For k in range(4)` — the loop that binds each lap as an
# ambient parameter while threading the world through. That is what lets the
# same four-cell walk be written once, as a `Part Entity`, and called by name
# from a key handler, from the timer and from the frame.

Innate Domain: Game Dev

Cursed Object: wellRows As 12
Cursed Object: wellCols As 6

Part World:
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> {rows: fill(12, repeat(".", 6)), piece: list(point(0, 1), point(0, 2), point(0, 3), point(0, 4)), try: list(point(0, 0), point(0, 0), point(0, 0), point(0, 0)), step: point(1, 0), ok: 1 = 1, stamp: 1 = 0, score: 0, over: 1 = 0}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The four-cell walks. Each takes the world and gives it back, so each is an
# ordinary Shikigami once the scope has lowered it.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Part Entity "Slide":
    # `try` becomes the piece moved by `step`.
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> with(w, "try", w.piece)
    Simple Domain: For k in range(4)
        Cursed Technique: Apply
            Using: (w, k) ->
                consider moved as padd(item(w.piece, k), w.step)
                in with(w, "try", set(w.try, k, moved))

Part Entity "Spin":
    # `try` becomes the piece turned a quarter turn about its second cell.
    # Any cell would do as a pivot; the second one is the middle of every
    # shape below, which keeps a rotation from wandering across the well.
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> with(w, "try", w.piece)
    Simple Domain: For k in range(4)
        Cursed Technique: Apply
            Using: (w, k) ->
                consider pivot as item(w.piece, 1)
                in consider p as item(w.piece, k)
                in consider turned as padd(pivot, point(pcol(p) - pcol(pivot), 0 - (prow(p) - prow(pivot))))
                in with(w, "try", set(w.try, k, turned))

Part Entity "Fits":
    # `ok` says whether `try` may be placed: inside the well, on empty cells.
    # `and` short-circuits, so the bounds are checked before `charat` is asked
    # for a row that is not there.
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> with(w, "ok", 1 = 1)
    Simple Domain: For k in range(4)
        Cursed Technique: Apply
            Using: (w, k) ->
                consider p as item(w.try, k)
                in with(w, "ok", w.ok
                    and prow(p) >= 0 and prow(p) < wellRows
                    and pcol(p) >= 0 and pcol(p) < wellCols
                    and charat(item(w.rows, prow(p)), pcol(p)) = ".")

Part Entity "Move":
    # Accept `try` if it fits, and leave the piece where it was if it does not.
    Shikigami: Fits
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> if w.ok then with(w, "piece", w.try) else w

Part Entity "Stamp":
    # Write the piece into the rows, when `stamp` says to. It is set on the
    # tick a piece comes to rest — and by `Part Draw:` on the copy it draws,
    # which is how a falling piece is visible without being part of the well.
    Simple Domain: For k in range(4)
        Cursed Technique: Apply
            Using: (w, k) ->
                if not(w.stamp)
                    then w
                    else consider p as item(w.piece, k)
                        in consider row as item(w.rows, prow(p))
                        in with(w, "rows", set(w.rows, prow(p), withchar(row, pcol(p), "#")))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# What the player does.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Part On "key left":
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> if w.over then w else with(w, "step", point(0, -1))
    Shikigami: Slide
    Shikigami: Move

Part On "key right":
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> if w.over then w else with(w, "step", point(0, 1))
    Shikigami: Slide
    Shikigami: Move

Part On "key down":
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> if w.over then w else with(w, "step", point(1, 0))
    Shikigami: Slide
    Shikigami: Move

Part On "key up":
    Shikigami: Spin
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> if w.over then with(w, "try", w.piece) else w
    Shikigami: Move

Part On "key q":
    Simple Domain: Quit

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# What time does: fall, or come to rest.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Part Every 400:
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> if w.over then w else with(w, "step", point(1, 0))
    Shikigami: Slide
    Shikigami: Fits
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> if w.over then w else if w.ok then with(w, "piece", w.try) else with(w, "stamp", 1 = 1)
    Shikigami: Stamp

    # A full row is one with no "." left in it. Walking downwards is enough
    # for a single pass: everything above a cleared row has already been
    # looked at, and what slides into its place is one of those.
    Simple Domain: For i in range(12)
        Cursed Technique: Apply
            Using: (w, i) ->
                if not(w.stamp) or indexof(item(w.rows, i), ".") >= 0
                    then w
                    else with(with(w, "rows", concat(concat(list(repeat(".", wellCols)), take(w.rows, i)), drop(w.rows, i + 1))),
                        "score", w.score + 100)

    # The next piece, and the question a new one asks: is there room?
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) ->
            if not(w.stamp)
                then w
                else with(w, "piece", pick(list(
                    list(point(0, 1), point(0, 2), point(0, 3), point(0, 4)),
                    list(point(0, 2), point(0, 3), point(1, 2), point(1, 3)),
                    list(point(0, 1), point(0, 2), point(0, 3), point(1, 2)),
                    list(point(0, 1), point(1, 1), point(2, 1), point(2, 2)),
                    list(point(0, 2), point(0, 3), point(1, 1), point(1, 2)))))
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> with(w, "try", w.piece)
    Shikigami: Fits
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> with(with(w, "over", w.over or (w.stamp and not(w.ok))), "stamp", 1 = 0)

Part Draw:
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> with(w, "stamp", 1 = 1)
    Shikigami: Stamp
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) ->
            stack(
                beside(text("score "), style(text(totext(w.score)), "bold yellow")),
                box(draw(w.rows)),
                text(if w.over then "game over" else "arrows move and turn, q quits"))

Part Ending:
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> "final score " + totext(w.score)
    Reveal: stdout

It is, through one form worth knowing: **`Consider NAME Of` takes a pipeline
body**, not only a lambda. So a stage whose value is the world can run a
whole search over one of its fields and keep the world:

Cursed Technique: Apply
Consider field Of
Cursed Technique: Apply
Using: (w) -> w.board
Channeled Energy: Convert To Grid
Domain Expansion: BFS from 4 12
Using: (c) -> not(c = "T")

# Tower defence — the game that asks whether the algorithm vocabulary is
# reachable from inside one.
#
# It is, through one form worth knowing: **`Consider NAME Of` takes a pipeline
# body**, not only a lambda. So a stage whose value is the world can run a
# whole search over one of its fields and keep the world:
#
#     Cursed Technique: Apply
#         Consider field Of
#             Cursed Technique: Apply
#                 Using: (w) -> w.board
#             Channeled Energy: Convert To Grid
#             Domain Expansion: BFS from 4 12
#                 Using: (c) -> not(c = "T")
#         Using: (w) -> with(w, "flow", field)
#
# That is the whole of the routing. `BFS` from the **exit** gives every cell
# its distance to safety, and a creep walks downhill — a flow field, computed
# by the same primitive a maze puzzle uses, with no path-finding written here
# at all. It is recomputed whenever a tower is placed, which is also how the
# rule "a tower may not seal the lane" is checked: if the entry's distance
# comes back below zero, there is no way through and the tower is refused.
#
# The creeps are a `List<Record>`, advanced each tick by `Simple Domain: For
# Each` — the loop this game motivated: a wave spawns creeps mid-game, so
# the list `w.creeps` grows while the game runs, and `For Each cr In: Using:
# (w) -> w.creeps` reads however many there are *this tick*, with no fixed
# slot count and no `k >= length(...)` guard standing in for one.

Innate Domain: Game Dev

Cursed Object: boardRows As 5
Cursed Object: boardCols As 13
Cursed Object: exitCol As 12
Cursed Object: towerCost As 10

Part World:
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Consider field Of
            Cursed Technique: Apply
                Using: (w) -> fill(5, repeat(".", 13))
            Channeled Energy: Convert To Grid
            Domain Expansion: BFS from 2 12
                Using: (c) -> not(c = "T")
        Using: (w) -> {board: fill(5, repeat(".", 13)), flow: field, creeps: emptylist({r: 0, c: 0, hp: 0}), cursor: point(2, 4), coin: 55, lives: 5, wave: 0, note: "arrows aim, enter builds a tower, q leaves", lines: emptylist("")}

Part Entity "Flow":
    # Every cell's distance to the exit, and the world with it in hand.
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Consider field Of
            Cursed Technique: Apply
                Using: (w) -> w.board
            Channeled Energy: Convert To Grid
            Domain Expansion: BFS from 2 12
                Using: (c) -> not(c = "T")
        Using: (w) -> with(w, "flow", field)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Building
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Part On "key up":
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> with(w, "cursor", point(clamp(prow(w.cursor) - 1, 0, boardRows - 1), pcol(w.cursor)))

Part On "key down":
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> with(w, "cursor", point(clamp(prow(w.cursor) + 1, 0, boardRows - 1), pcol(w.cursor)))

Part On "key left":
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> with(w, "cursor", point(prow(w.cursor), clamp(pcol(w.cursor) - 1, 0, boardCols - 1)))

Part On "key right":
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> with(w, "cursor", point(prow(w.cursor), clamp(pcol(w.cursor) + 1, 0, boardCols - 1)))

Part On "key enter":
    # Put the tower down, then ask the search whether the lane survived it.
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) ->
            consider r as prow(w.cursor)
            in consider c as pcol(w.cursor)
            in consider row as item(w.board, r)
            in if w.coin < towerCost
                then with(w, "note", "Not enough coin — a tower is 10.")
                else if not(charat(row, c) = ".")
                then with(w, "note", "Something is there already.")
                else with(with(with(w, "board", set(w.board, r, withchar(row, c, "T"))), "coin", w.coin - towerCost),
                    "note", "A tower goes up.")
    Shikigami: Flow
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) ->
            if at(w.flow, 2, 0) >= 0
                then w
                else consider r as prow(w.cursor)
                    in consider c as pcol(w.cursor)
                    in consider row as item(w.board, r)
                    in with(with(with(w, "board", set(w.board, r, withchar(row, c, "."))), "coin", w.coin + towerCost),
                        "note", "That would seal the lane. The tower comes down again.")
    Shikigami: Flow

Part On "key q":
    Simple Domain: Quit

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A wave every two seconds
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Part Every 2000:
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) ->
            if w.lives <= 0
                then w
                else with(with(with(w, "wave", w.wave + 1), "creeps",
                        concat(w.creeps, list({r: 2, c: 0, hp: 2 + w.wave}))),
                    "note", "Wave " + totext(w.wave + 1) + " comes up the lane.")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A step every half second: shoot, walk, tally
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Part Every 500:
    # Every tower fires at every creep within two cells of it. The outer lap
    # is `For Each`, over however many creeps are alive this tick; the inner
    # one is `For`, over every cell of the board. `snapshot` (the element
    # `For Each` hands the body) is deliberately unused below — two towers
    # can both be in range of the same creep, so each `t` still re-reads the
    # creep fresh via `k` (the index `For Each` hands alongside it), or the
    # second tower's hit would overwrite the first's instead of stacking.
    Simple Domain: For Each snapshot In
        Using: (w) -> w.creeps
        Simple Domain: For t in range(65)
            Cursed Technique: Apply
                Using: (w, snapshot, k, t) ->
                    consider cr as item(w.creeps, k)
                    in consider tr as t / boardCols
                    in consider tc as mod(t, boardCols)
                    in if not(charat(item(w.board, tr), tc) = "T")
                        or chebyshev(point(cr.r, cr.c), point(tr, tc)) > 2
                        or cr.hp <= 0
                        then w
                        else with(w, "creeps", set(w.creeps, k, with(cr, "hp", cr.hp - 1)))

    # Everything still standing walks one cell downhill. `cr` and `k` are the
    # element and index `For Each` hands the body — nothing else in this loop
    # writes to another creep's slot, so the element ambient stays fresh for
    # the whole lap and there is no need to re-read it as the shoot loop above
    # does.
    Simple Domain: For Each cr In
        Using: (w) -> w.creeps
        Cursed Technique: Apply
            Using: (w, cr, k) ->
                consider up as (if inbounds(w.flow, cr.r - 1, cr.c) and at(w.flow, cr.r - 1, cr.c) >= 0 then at(w.flow, cr.r - 1, cr.c) else 999)
                in consider down as (if inbounds(w.flow, cr.r + 1, cr.c) and at(w.flow, cr.r + 1, cr.c) >= 0 then at(w.flow, cr.r + 1, cr.c) else 999)
                in consider left as (if inbounds(w.flow, cr.r, cr.c - 1) and at(w.flow, cr.r, cr.c - 1) >= 0 then at(w.flow, cr.r, cr.c - 1) else 999)
                in consider right as (if inbounds(w.flow, cr.r, cr.c + 1) and at(w.flow, cr.r, cr.c + 1) >= 0 then at(w.flow, cr.r, cr.c + 1) else 999)
                in consider best as min(list(up, down, left, right))
                in consider next as (if right = best then point(cr.r, cr.c + 1)
                    else if up = best then point(cr.r - 1, cr.c)
                    else if down = best then point(cr.r + 1, cr.c)
                    else point(cr.r, cr.c - 1))
                in if cr.hp <= 0 or best >= 999
                    then w
                    else with(w, "creeps", set(w.creeps, k, with(with(cr, "r", prow(next)), "c", pcol(next))))

    # What is left of the lane. Three filters over one list, each naming what
    # it wants — the shape `Consider … Of` was made for.
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Consider standing Of
            Cursed Technique: Apply
                Using: (w) -> w.creeps
            Cursed Technique: Filter
                Using: (cr) -> cr.hp > 0 and cr.c < exitCol
        Consider killed Of
            Cursed Technique: Apply
                Using: (w) -> w.creeps
            Cursed Technique: Filter
                Using: (cr) -> cr.hp <= 0
        Consider leaked Of
            Cursed Technique: Apply
                Using: (w) -> w.creeps
            Cursed Technique: Filter
                Using: (cr) -> cr.hp > 0 and cr.c >= exitCol
        Using: (w) ->
            with(with(with(with(w, "creeps", standing),
                    "coin", w.coin + length(killed) * 6),
                "lives", w.lives - length(leaked)),
                "note", if length(leaked) > 0
                    then "One got through."
                    else if length(killed) > 0

                    else w.note)

        Using: (w) -> with(w, "lines", w.board)

    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) ->
            stack(
                beside(text("coin "), style(text(totext(w.coin)), "bold yellow"),
                    text("   lives "), style(text(totext(w.lives)), "bold red"),
                    text("   wave "), text(totext(w.wave))),
                box(draw(w.lines)),
                text(if w.lives <= 0 then "the lane is lost" else w.note))

Part Ending:
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> "held for " + totext(w.wave) + " wave(s) with " + totext(w.lives) + " lives left"

source:
# Wordle, against a room on a server — the game that has to talk to something
# it does not control.
#
# A round trip is a hundred milliseconds on a good day and a frame is sixteen,
# so a `Request` **fires and returns the world unchanged**. The answer arrives
# later at `Part Reply "guess":`, which is an event like a keystroke. That is
# the whole of the asynchrony, and it is why nothing here blocks.
#
# There is no server in this directory and there does not need to be. A
# replayed run never touches the network: the script says what came back, so
# the two halves of an exchange are two lines of a file. `reply guess {…}` is a
# room that answered and `fail guess …` is one that did not, and a request the
# script never answers is a room that went away mid-game — which is a state
# worth testing and has no other way to be tested at all.

Innate Domain: Game Dev

Part World:
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> {room: "oak-42", typed: "", guesses: emptylist(""), marks: emptylist(""), lines: emptylist(""), note: "five letters, then enter", spin: 0, over: 1 = 0}

# Typing. A printable keystroke arrives as `text`, which is a different
# question from `key` — one asks what was pressed, the other what it wrote.
Part On "text":
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) ->
            if w.over or length(w.typed) >= 5 or not(isalpha(key))
                then w
                else with(w, "typed", w.typed + lower(key))

Part On "key backspace":
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> with(w, "typed", slice(w.typed, 0, length(w.typed) - 1))

# Enter sends the guess to the room. `pending` is how the one thing a bounded
# tag costs — a superseded reply is dropped — is made visible, so a game that
# must not lose one asks before it fires.
Part On "key enter":
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) ->
            if w.over or not(length(w.typed) = 5)
                then with(w, "note", "five letters, then enter")
                else if pending("guess")
                then with(w, "note", "still waiting on the room")
                else with(w, "note", "asking the room about " + upper(w.typed) + "…")
    Domain Expansion: Request
        Url: (w) -> "https://wordle.example/room/" + w.room + "/guess"
        Method: "POST"
        Body: (w) -> tojson({room: w.room, word: w.typed})
        As: "guess"
        Into: {marks: Text, right: Bool, left: Int}

Part On "key q":
    Simple Domain: Quit

# The answer, whenever it comes. Every way the exchange can fail lands in the
# same record — the room is down, the status was not 2xx, the body did not fit
# the declared shape — so there is one thing to branch on.
Part Reply "guess":
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) ->
            if not(reply.ok)
                then with(w, "note", "the room is not answering (" + reply.error + ")")
                else with(with(with(with(with(w,
                        "guesses", concat(w.guesses, list(w.typed))),
                        "marks", concat(w.marks, list(reply.value.marks))),
                        "typed", ""),
                        "over", reply.value.right or reply.value.left <= 0),
                    "note", if reply.value.right
                        then "got it"
                        else if reply.value.left <= 0
                        then "out of guesses"
                        else totext(reply.value.left) + " left")

# A spinner, so a frame drawn while a request is out looks like it is waiting
# rather than like it is stuck.
Part Every 250:
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> with(w, "spin", mod(w.spin + 1, 4))

Part Draw:
    # One line per guess: the word, then what the room said about it.
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> with(w, "lines", emptylist(""))
    Simple Domain: For k in range(6)
        Cursed Technique: Apply
            Using: (w, k) ->
                if k >= length(w.guesses)
                    then w
                    else with(w, "lines", concat(w.lines,
                        list(upper(item(w.guesses, k)) + "   " + item(w.marks, k))))
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) ->
            box(stack(
                beside(style(text("WORDLE"), "bold"), text("   room "), style(text(w.room), "cyan")),
                margin(text(textjoin(w.lines, "\n")), 0, 1),
                beside(
                    text("> "),
                    style(text(upper(w.typed) + repeat("_", 5 - length(w.typed))), "bold yellow"),
                    text(if pending("guess") then "  " + charat("|/-\\", w.spin) else "")),
                text(w.note)))

Part Ending:
    Cursed Technique: Apply
        Using: (w) -> totext(length(w.guesses)) + " guess(es), " + (if w.over then "finished" else "unfinished")
    Reveal: stdout
